finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled Base64 data to Marshal.load, allowing unsafe deserialization and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: params[:state] from the POST /restore request (form or query parameter), unauthenticated, public Sinatra route

trace.note: Public route post '/restore' defined with no authentication filter
params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load, which instantiates arbitrary objects
state.inspect is returned, so the response also leaks object contents

finding.guards_checked: No before filters, auth, or signature/HMAC check on the payload. No class allowlist. Marshal.load has no safe mode. Sinatra defaults offer no protection here. This is the only source file. Sinatra's Rack::Protection does not block this.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 defines a public, unauthenticated POST /restore with no filters, and passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load, which has no allowlist or signature check, and app.rb:7 returns state.inspect. app.rb is the only source file.
